title: Lodewijk van Toulon to Dirk van Hogendorp, 30 July 1803 (NA 1.02.13 inv. 208; DECODE R2034)

steps.what: Fetched the private DECODE R2034 image using the supplied session cookie and produced lossless inspection derivatives.
Transcribed all 110 numerical groups and their superscript series marks from the manuscript.
Checked exact names/date, Tomokiyo's Cryptiana, the 1943 brotherly correspondence, Sillem's 1890 biography, and the HistoCrypt 2026 paper and repository.
Located the archival description of the reused 1799/1801/1803 Correspondentiecijffer explicitly annotated for Van Hogendorp in St Petersburg.
Applied the photographed 5 August 1803 inventory-228 codebook (DECODE R1035) group by group; its entries yield disconnected dictionary words and none of its Begin controls occurs in R2034.

Aligned the contemporary plaintext solutions of same-key Bourdeaux dispatches R1944 and R1946 (1801) with their ciphertext; mark-sensitive matches give 51~ van, 279 en, 153 Paul, 222= niet, 43~ zyne, 304~ wegens, 380~ de in R2034.
Sillem 1890 quotes 'zoo wonderlijk' from same-key R1942 (no. 12, 5 July 1803); the unique adjacent pair 907^ 934" gives zoo and wonderlijk.

Transcribed all 187 groups of same-key R1945 (3 Feb 1801) and set them against its 152-word contemporary solution. Only one base+mark group (222=) is shared with R2034's meaningful part. The one-to-one alignment drifts (repeated groups 273~, 733~, 916=, 977= fall on different words), so no new R2034 value can be fixed.

Checked whether values within each marked series are alphabetical, using R1946's recovered pairs (e.g. ~ series: 297 Men, 370 Heer, 500 dat, 580 de, 733 zeer, 884 waar). They are not, so page-order/monotone-alphabet attacks do not apply.
Re-read R2034 from the DECODE image at full zoom; ten groups corrected (336~, 897", 880^, 859~, 528-, 145^, 616+, 215-, 625-, 188-).

Applied Van Kampen's full 1,849-entry R1035 nomenclator under all 2,520 mark mappings; coverage at or below a random-mark baseline (22% vs 28%); the best mapping's "met Zijne Keizerlijke Majesteit" is an artefact. R1942 also at chance against R1035.
Checked unvisited Batavian DECODE records R1926, R1947, R2053, R1033: per-digit marks, four-digit groups or the R1035 book; none uses key 34313.
Transcribed same-key R1946 (202 groups) and R1944 (115 groups) in full and aligned them with their contemporary solutions; R1946 aligns one-to-one to word 150, confirmed by 153= Paul and 222= niet.

Checked the 20-21 Sept anchors against the full transcriptions: 51~ van, 279 en, 153 Paul, 43~ zyne, 304~ wegens, 380~ de do not occur where claimed (R1946 van = 444=/957~, wegens = 564~, Paul = 153= not bare 153); withdrawn.
Looked up every R2034 group in the four same-key transcriptions: 222- niet and 394 handen (R1946, high), 58 brengen (R1944, medium); 907^ zoo / 934" wonderlijk kept as a conjecture from Sillem.
Re-tested R1038 (1765) since its rejection used the withdrawn anchors: no entry for niet, handen or brengen, and it marks digits, not groups.

outcome.method_basis: The key is identified archivally (NA 2.21.045/34313, a booklet not digitised), and full transcriptions of the same-key 1801 letters R1944/R1946 with their contemporary solutions fix only 3 of R2034's 67 words; the rest cannot be recovered without the book.
outcome.notes: Attempted, open. The key survives only as a physical booklet (NA 2.21.045/34313; dup. 2.21.227/335; Museum B1 392). Full transcriptions of same-key R1944 and R1946 (1801) fix 3 of 67 words (222- niet, 394 handen, 58 brengen); the nine values claimed on 20-21 Sept were not reproducible and were withdrawn. The series are not alphabetical, so the rest cannot be recovered without the book.
outcome.fraction_read_source: partial_solution.md: 3 of the 67 text groups between the controls 430~ and 763~ fixed from same-key plaintext

gaps.detail: key survives only as NA 2.21.045/34313, not digitised; the solved same-key letters R1944-R1946 do not contain these groups

prior.where: DECODE marks R2034 non-decrypted; no printed solution found

human: Provided the authenticated DECODE session cookie and selected the target.
